numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For length-2 inputs where one input is constant, `scipy.stats.pearsonr([1, 1], [2, 3])` issues a `ConstantInputWarning` but returns `PearsonRResult(statistic=np.float64(0.0), pvalue=np.float64(1.0))` instead of `nan` values.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For the same inputs, return `PearsonRResult(statistic=nan, pvalue=nan)` (while still raising a `ConstantInputWarning`).
trigger_conditions: Pearson correlation with n==2 (input arrays of length two)
At least one input is constant

input_output_examples.source: pr_body:PR#21763 and diff of scipy/stats/_stats_py.py around the n==2 handling
pr_body:PR#21763 shows both the incorrect and corrected outputs

oracle_clues: The documentation quoted in the PR states that when there is one or more constant inputs, `stats.pearsonr` returns `np.nan` as well as raising a warning.
The PR explicitly says the special case `length two` was not working and shows the incorrect vs corrected `PearsonRResult` values.
A later suggestion/implementation discussion notes the goal to “return exact 1.0 or -1.0 values for n == 2 case” and to handle n==2 constant inputs correctly.

category_specific_evidence: Violation of documented mathematical/behavioral property for Pearson correlation when n == 2: for constant input, the correlation coefficient is not defined, so pearsonr should return NaN (both statistic and pvalue) rather than finite values.

Concrete demonstrating values from passage PR#21763: stats.pearsonr([1, 1], [2, 3]) originally returned PearsonRResult(statistic=np.float64(0.0), pvalue=np.float64(1.0)) even though one input is constant and a ConstantInputWarning is raised.
Concrete expected outcome shown in passage PR#21763 for the same input: stats.pearsonr([1, 1], [2, 3]) now returns PearsonRResult(statistic=nan, pvalue=nan).

Additional concrete test values from passage test_length_two_constant_input: x = xp.asarray([0.667, 0.667]) (zero variance/constant), y = xp.asarray([0.123, 0.456]); with pytest.warns(stats.ConstantInputWarning, match='An input array is constant'), stats.pearsonr(x, y) must satisfy r == xp.nan and p == xp.nan via xp_assert_close.
reproduction_risks: JAX backend differences: tests are marked @skip_xp_backends('jax.numpy', reason='JAX doesn't allow item assignment.'), so reproductions on jax.numpy may fail due to implementation constraints rather than the numerical correctness issue.
The example specifically targets the special case of input length n == 2; reproductions must use length-2 vectors (not other lengths) to trigger the documented n==2 behavior.
